text.p: Sierra Leone sprinter Horace Dove-Edwin, banned for four years after a positive drugs test at the 1994 Victoria Commonwealth Games, has been granted a request for an early reinstatement.
Dove-Edwin tested positive for the steroid stanozolol after finishing second to Briton Linford Christie in the 100 metres final.
In a statement released on Monday, the International Amateur Athletic Federation said its council had accepted a request from Dove-Edwin for early reinstatement.
IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reineri said Dove-Edwin had been reinstated on compassionate grounds.
"He was living in the United States and was unable to get a hearing in Sierra Leone until early this year," Reineri said. "Their federation upheld the ban but recommended an early reinstatement."
